summary.problem: The floating sidebar had a lower z-index (80) than the top-right toolbar buttons (100), so those buttons visually appeared on top of the open sidebar. Moving the sidebar above them (z-index 120) introduced a new problem: on mobile, the main menu dropdown would open behind the sidebar.
summary.solution: Raise the sidebar z-index above all toolbar UI, then close the floating sidebar automatically when the hamburger button is clicked. That second step required reworking how the dropdown trigger suppresses outside-click events — replacing a global attribute-based escape hatch with a scoped DOM-containment check.

plain.title: Sidebar above buttons, and closing it when the menu opens
plain.problem: The sidebar appeared behind toolbar buttons in the top-right corner. Fixing that by raising its layer made the main menu disappear behind the sidebar on mobile.
plain.fix: Raise the sidebar above all toolbar UI. Then auto-close the floating sidebar when the hamburger button is pressed, so the menu is always visible. Adjust the 'outside click' logic so the menu doesn't immediately close itself when its own trigger is tapped.

steps.title: Toolbar buttons render above the open sidebar
steps.headline: Toolbar buttons appeared on top of the sidebar
steps.say: When the sidebar was open, the buttons in the top-right corner of the toolbar sat visually on top of it. Clicking those buttons while the sidebar was open worked, but it looked broken — the buttons hovered over the panel.
steps.narration: The sidebar is a floating panel that slides in from the right. But the toolbar buttons in the top-right corner had a higher stacking order, so they painted on top of the open sidebar. The fix described in the pull request is to move the sidebar above those buttons.

beats.heading: How z-indices were arranged
beats.text: Before the PR, `--zIndex-ui-library` was 80, placed between the bottom bar (60) and the context menu (90). The top toolbar's `--zIndex-ui-top` was 100 — higher than the sidebar.

lines.annotation: Sidebar z-index: below context-menu and ui-top.
App top-bar z-index: same as styles-popup, above sidebar.

steps.title: Raise sidebar z-index above all toolbar UI
steps.headline: Sidebar z-index raised above all toolbar buttons
steps.say: The sidebar z-index is bumped from 80 to 120 — above the 100 used by both the top bar and the styles popup. It's repositioned in the token list to make the ordering obvious.
steps.narration: The fix for buttons appearing above the sidebar is straightforward: raise the sidebar's z-index number. It moves from 80 to 120, which puts it above every toolbar element. In the token list it also moves to the bottom of the UI group so the ascending order is easy to read.

beats.heading: The token value and its position both change
beats.text: `--zIndex-ui-library` jumps from 80 to 120, and its line moves to after the 100-level entries so the list reads in ascending order.

lines.annotation: 120 > 100: sidebar now paints above the top bar and styles popup.

steps.title: On mobile, the main menu now opens behind the sidebar
steps.headline: Higher z-index makes the menu hide behind the sidebar on mobile
steps.say: Now that the sidebar sits above everything at z-index 120, the main menu dropdown — which is rendered in the normal document flow with a local z-index of 2 — appears underneath the sidebar when both are open at the same time on a phone.
steps.check: On desktop the sidebar is docked or sits beside the canvas, so the menu and sidebar don't overlap. Is mobile-only overlap actually what prompts this concern?
steps.narration: Raising the sidebar fixes the desktop overlap but creates a new problem on mobile. The sidebar renders before the top bar in the mobile layout, and the dropdown menu content only has an internal z-index of 2. With the sidebar now at 120, opening the hamburger menu while the sidebar is visible puts the menu behind the panel. The PR description calls this out explicitly.

beats.heading: Render order on mobile
beats.text: In `MobileMenu`, `renderSidebars()` is called first — before the top bar — so the sidebar element appears earlier in the DOM. With `z-index: 120` it paints over the menu content whose local stacking context only reaches `z-index: 2`.

lines.annotation: Sidebar rendered first → sidebar stacking context established before the top bar.

{/* ordered in this reverse order so that top bar is on top */}

notes: Whether this is visible on desktop is not confirmed — on desktop the sidebar is docked or rendered beside the canvas and unlikely to overlap the hamburger button. This is an inferred mobile-only issue from the PR description.

steps.title: Auto-close the floating sidebar when the hamburger is tapped
steps.headline: Tapping the hamburger now auto-closes the floating sidebar
steps.say: Instead of trying to raise the menu above the sidebar, the PR simply closes the floating sidebar when the hamburger is pressed. The sidebar already closes itself on any outside click — so the fix is to stop suppressing that outside-click when the hamburger button is the target.
steps.narration: The sidebar has always used a 'close on outside click' hook. But the hamburger button carried a special attribute that told that hook to ignore clicks on it. Removing that attribute means clicking the hamburger is now treated as an outside click by the sidebar, which closes the panel before the menu opens. This is the core decision of the PR.

beats.heading: How the trigger suppressed outside-click previously
beats.text: `data-prevent-outside-click` on the trigger button told `useOutsideClick` to skip any click whose target was inside an element bearing that attribute. The sidebar's hook respected it, so clicking the hamburger never closed the sidebar.

lines.annotation: Opt-out from all useOutsideClick listeners in the page — including the sidebar's.

lines.text: // clicking on a container that ignores outside clicks

lines.annotation: Any element with this attribute anywhere in the page exempts itself from ALL outside-click listeners.

beats.heading: Remove the attribute from the trigger
beats.text: Dropping `data-prevent-outside-click` means a click on the hamburger is no longer exempted. The sidebar's `useOutsideClick` fires, calls `closeLibrary()`, and the sidebar closes before the menu opens.

lines.annotation: Removed: hamburger clicks are now visible to every useOutsideClick listener, including the sidebar's.

steps.title: Without the attribute the menu closes itself on the trigger click
steps.headline: Removing the attribute breaks the menu toggle
steps.say: The dropdown menu also uses `useOutsideClick` to close itself. With the attribute gone, clicking the trigger is seen as an outside-click by the menu content, so the menu opens and immediately closes — the toggle stops working.
steps.narration: The same attribute that protected the sidebar also protected the dropdown menu. The menu content listens for outside clicks to close itself, and the trigger button was its own exemption. Without the attribute, tapping the hamburger causes the menu to open from the click handler, then immediately close from the outside-click handler. We need a more precise guard that only prevents the menu from closing when its own trigger is the click target.

beats.heading: What breaks when the attribute is removed
beats.text: The `MenuContent` component uses `useOutsideClick` to call `onClickOutside` (which closes the menu). Before, the trigger's `data-prevent-outside-click` exempted it. Without it, clicking the trigger fires both `onClick` (open) and `useOutsideClick` callback (close).

lines.annotation: Fires for any click outside menuRef — including a click on the trigger button.

steps.title: Wrap trigger+content in a container; check containment instead of attribute
steps.headline: A shared wrapper lets the menu check its own trigger precisely
steps.say: A new `div.dropdown-menu-container` wraps both the trigger button and the menu panel. When an outside click fires, the menu content checks whether the click target is inside that shared wrapper. If it is, the click is on the trigger, so the menu stays open and the toggle logic handles it.
steps.check: `DropdownMenuContent` already uses `className="dropdown-menu-container"` internally for the Island/Stack wrapper. Now `DropdownMenu` also wraps the outer element with the same class. Does the `closest()` call stop at the right level?
steps.narration: Instead of a page-wide attribute escape hatch, the trigger and the content are now siblings inside a single wrapper element. The content's outside-click callback walks up from the clicked element to see if it lands inside that wrapper. If it does, the click is on the trigger — so no close. This is scoped entirely to one dropdown instance and doesn't suppress any other listeners on the page.

beats.heading: DropdownMenu wraps its children
beats.text: The fragment `<>…</>` is replaced by a `div` with `className="dropdown-menu-container"` and `display: contents` so it has no layout effect.

lines.text: // remove this div from box layout

lines.annotation: `display: contents` makes this div invisible to the layout engine — no extra box is created.

beats.heading: Content checks containment instead of attribute
beats.text: The outside-click callback now walks from the content's own element to its nearest `.dropdown-menu-container` ancestor and checks whether the click target is inside it. A trigger click is always inside, so it is ignored.

lines.text: // prevents closing if clicking on the trigger button

lines.annotation: Walks up from the menu panel to find its shared wrapper.
If the click target is inside the wrapper (i.e. on the trigger), do not close.

steps.title: useOutsideClick callback receives typed event target
steps.headline: Outside-click callback now knows the target element type
steps.say: The `useOutsideClick` callback signature previously typed the event as plain `Event`. The new `DropdownMenuContent` guard calls `event.target` with DOM methods on it, so the signature is narrowed to carry a typed `target` field.
steps.narration: The new outside-click guard in the menu content calls `.contains()` on the event target, which requires a typed reference. The hook signature is updated to reflect what the implementation already cast internally, making the new call site type-safe.

beats.heading: Callback type narrows `event.target`
beats.text: The callback parameter type goes from `Event` to `Event & { target: T }`, matching the internal cast that was already there.

pr.title: fix: close floating sidebar on main menu open
pr.author: dwelle
commitTitles: fix: close floating sidebar on main menu open
pr.body:
- move sidebar above top layer UI (especially top-right) so that buttons aren't above the sidebar when open
- close sidebar (when not docked) when opening main menu. This is necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile.
